# Harness configuration

<!-- Generated by `node mcp-wrapper/cli.mjs config --markdown`. Edit mcp-wrapper/harnesses.mjs, then regenerate. -->

Every harness below runs the same server, `node /ABS/PATH/elm-lsp-rust/mcp-wrapper/index.mjs`.
Replace `/ABS/PATH` with the directory that holds your clone, or run `node mcp-wrapper/cli.mjs config <harness>`
to print the entry with the path filled in.

If a harness reports that it cannot find `node`, replace `node` with the output of `command -v node`.
Editors started from a desktop launcher often do not see the `PATH` of your shell.

## Claude Code

With your paths filled in: `node mcp-wrapper/cli.mjs config claude-code`

- project: `.mcp.json`
- user: `~/.claude.json`

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "elm-lsp": {
      "command": "node",
      "args": [
        "/ABS/PATH/elm-lsp-rust/mcp-wrapper/index.mjs"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Or run:

```sh
claude mcp add --scope user elm-lsp -- node /ABS/PATH/elm-lsp-rust/mcp-wrapper/index.mjs
```

Run `claude mcp list`, or `/mcp` inside a session.

The Claude Code plugin is an alternative. It registers the server and the skill in one step: `/plugin marketplace add CharlonTank/elm-lsp-plugin`, then `/plugin install elm-lsp-rust@CharlonTank/elm-lsp-plugin`.

Source: <https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp>

## OpenAI Codex

With your paths filled in: `node mcp-wrapper/cli.mjs config codex`

- project: `.codex/config.toml`
- user: `~/.codex/config.toml`

```toml
[mcp_servers.elm-lsp]
command = "node"
args = ["/ABS/PATH/elm-lsp-rust/mcp-wrapper/index.mjs"]
```

Or run:

```sh
codex mcp add elm-lsp -- node /ABS/PATH/elm-lsp-rust/mcp-wrapper/index.mjs
```

Run `codex mcp list`, or `/mcp` inside a session.

Codex reads the project file only in trusted projects.

Codex starts MCP servers with a reduced environment. `PATH` is passed on. List anything else the Elm compiler needs under `env_vars`.

Source: <https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/extend/mcp>

## GitHub Copilot (CLI and VS Code)

With your paths filled in: `node mcp-wrapper/cli.mjs config copilot`

- project: `.mcp.json`
- user: `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json`

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "elm-lsp": {
      "type": "local",
      "command": "node",
      "args": [
        "/ABS/PATH/elm-lsp-rust/mcp-wrapper/index.mjs"
      ],
      "tools": [
        "*"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Or run:

```sh
copilot mcp add elm-lsp -- node /ABS/PATH/elm-lsp-rust/mcp-wrapper/index.mjs
```

Run `copilot mcp list`. In VS Code, run **MCP: List Servers** from the Command Palette.

VS Code's older Local harness reads `.vscode/mcp.json` instead. There the top-level key is `servers` and the entry has no `tools` field.

Source: <https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-cli/customize-copilot/add-mcp-servers>

## OpenCode

With your paths filled in: `node mcp-wrapper/cli.mjs config opencode`

- project: `opencode.json`
- user: `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "mcp": {
    "servers": {
      "elm-lsp": {
        "type": "local",
        "command": [
          "node",
          "/ABS/PATH/elm-lsp-rust/mcp-wrapper/index.mjs"
        ]
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Or run:

```sh
opencode mcp add elm-lsp -- node /ABS/PATH/elm-lsp-rust/mcp-wrapper/index.mjs
```

Run `opencode mcp list`.

OpenCode 1.x has no `servers` level. Put the `elm-lsp` entry directly under `mcp`, and use the file instead of `opencode mcp add`, which is interactive there.

Source: <https://opencode.ai/docs/mcp-servers/>

## Cline

With your paths filled in: `node mcp-wrapper/cli.mjs config cline`

- user: `~/.cline/data/settings/cline_mcp_settings.json`

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "elm-lsp": {
      "command": "node",
      "args": [
        "/ABS/PATH/elm-lsp-rust/mcp-wrapper/index.mjs"
      ],
      "disabled": false,
      "autoApprove": []
    }
  }
}
```

Or run:

```sh
cline mcp add elm-lsp --yes -- node /ABS/PATH/elm-lsp-rust/mcp-wrapper/index.mjs
```

Run `cline config mcp`, or open the **MCP Servers** panel of the extension.

In the extension, **MCP Servers** > **Configure** > **Configure MCP Servers** opens the file.

Source: <https://docs.cline.bot/mcp/configuring-mcp-servers>

## Goose

With your paths filled in: `node mcp-wrapper/cli.mjs config goose`

- user: `~/.config/goose/config.yaml`

```yaml
extensions:
  elm-lsp:
    name: elm-lsp
    type: stdio
    enabled: true
    cmd: "node"
    args: ["/ABS/PATH/elm-lsp-rust/mcp-wrapper/index.mjs"]
    timeout: 300
```

Or run:

```sh
goose session --with-extension 'node /ABS/PATH/elm-lsp-rust/mcp-wrapper/index.mjs'
```

Run `goose info -v`.

The command above adds the server to one session only. Edit the file, or run `goose configure` and pick **Add Extension** > **Command-Line Extension**, to keep it.

Source: <https://goose-docs.ai/docs/getting-started/using-extensions>

## Pi

With your paths filled in: `node mcp-wrapper/cli.mjs config pi`

- project: `.pi/mcp.json`
- user: `~/.pi/agent/mcp.json`

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "elm-lsp": {
      "command": "node",
      "args": [
        "/ABS/PATH/elm-lsp-rust/mcp-wrapper/index.mjs"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Or run:

```sh
pi mcp add elm-lsp -- node /ABS/PATH/elm-lsp-rust/mcp-wrapper/index.mjs
```

Run `pi mcp list`, or `/mcp` inside a session.

Pi calls MCP tools from codemode scripts by default. Add `"exposure": "direct"` to the entry to declare them to the model like built-in tools.

Source: <https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/main/packages/coding-agent/docs/mcp.md>

## Oh My Pi

With your paths filled in: `node mcp-wrapper/cli.mjs config oh-my-pi`

- project: `.omp/mcp.json`
- user: `~/.omp/agent/mcp.json`

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "elm-lsp": {
      "type": "stdio",
      "command": "node",
      "args": [
        "/ABS/PATH/elm-lsp-rust/mcp-wrapper/index.mjs"
      ]
```

Run `/mcp list` inside a session.

Oh My Pi also picks up servers that Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode or Cursor already have configured.

Source: <https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/blob/main/docs/mcp-config.md>

## Aider

With your paths filled in: `node mcp-wrapper/cli.mjs config aider`

```
/run node /ABS/PATH/elm-lsp-rust/mcp-wrapper/cli.mjs elm_references --file_path src/Main.elm --line 10 --character 4
```

Run `/run node /ABS/PATH/elm-lsp-rust/mcp-wrapper/cli.mjs doctor` inside a session.

Aider has no MCP client, so it uses the command-line interface. `/run` executes a command and offers to add its output to the chat.

Load the tool reference as read-only context with `aider --read /ABS/PATH/elm-lsp-rust/skills/elm-refactoring/SKILL.md`.

Source: <https://aider.chat/docs/usage/commands.html>
